sentences.text:
THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT 1.

This appeal is filed under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, (hereinafter referred to as 'MV Act' for brevity) by the appellants-claimants challenging the judgment and award dated 03.06.2015, passed in MVC No.457/2013, on the file of Senior Civil Judge and Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Kundapura (hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal' for brevity) seeking enhancement.

entities.text: Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Kundapura
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Brief facts:
On 03.02.2013 at about 2.30 p.m. the deceased G. Vasantha Nayak was riding his motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-20-R-992 from Mullikatte side towards Gangolli side and after reaching Nayakwadi Gopal Nayak's house in NC: 2023:KHC:20789 Gujjadi village, Kundapura taluk, a motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-20-EA-5612 belonging to respondent No.1 was driven by its rider in rash and negligent manner from Mullikatte side towards Gangolli side and dashed to motor cycle, due to said impact G. Vasantha Nayak sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries on the way to hospital.
3. Hence, a claim petition was filed by the appellant under Section-166 of the M.V. Act, claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in the accident.

The Tribunal on appreciating the materials on record, allowed the petition in part, and awarded compensation of Rs.18,32,200/-, along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The Tribunal held respondent Nos.1 and 2 therein, jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

4. Heard arguments of the learned counsel for the appellants and the learned counsel for respondent No.2 - insurance company and perused the materials on record.

sentences.text: The learned counsel for the appellants submitted that the quantum of compensation awarded under various heads is on lesser side.
Therefore, seeks for enhancement of the compensation.

6. On the other hand, the learned counsel appearing for the second respondent - insurance company submits that the Tribunal is justified in passing the impugned judgment and award and there is no ground for enhancement.
That the compensation amount as awarded by the Tribunal is sufficient and adequate.

7. The compensation awarded by the Tribunal is as follows:
Loss of dependency Rs. 17,47,200/-
 Consortium Rs. 25,000/-
 Love and affection Rs. 20,000/-
 Loss of estate Rs. 20,000/-
 Conveyance and funeral Rs. 20,000/-
 expenses

The Tribunal has taken the monthly income as Rs.12,000/- per month and adopted the multiplier of '14' since the deceased was 33 years old and added 30% of income towards loss of future prospects and appellants were granted compensation of Rs.17,47,200/- under the head 'loss of dependency'.
9.
The Insurance Company has challenged the quantum as well as liability imposed on it before the Division Bench of this Court in M.F.A. No.6168/2015.

The Division Bench of this Court in M.F.A. No.6168/2015 at para 14 observed regarding quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal and held that the compensation awarded to appellants - claimants is just and proper as all the parameters are taken correctly.
Therefore, the Division Bench of this Court has already confirmed the quantum of compensation assessed by the Tribunal.
It is found that all the parameters taken by the Tribunal while assessing the compensation are found to be correct.

Therefore,
there is no good ground available for enhancement of the NC: 2023:KHC:20789 compensation.
Even in the absence of proof of income, the Tribunal has taken the notional income at Rs.12,000/-

3 per month, whereas, as per Karnataka State Legal Services Authority chart, the monthly income ought to have been taken at Rs.8,000/-.

sentences.text: Therefore, the monthly income taken by the Tribunal is also found to be correct.
Therefore, there is no good ground available for enhancement of compensation.

10. Accordingly, I pass the following :
ORDER i.
The appeal is dismissed.
ii. The impugned judgment and award dated 03.06.2015, passed in MVC No.457/2013, on the file of Senior Civil Judge and Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Kundapura, is hereby confirmed.
